questions.question: A vertical mirror image of a figure swaps:
questions.rationale: A mirror standing upright reflects across a vertical axis: left becomes right, right becomes left, while top and bottom stay put. An option with BOTH swapped is a 180-degree rotation - the classic planted trap.

questions.question: A water image of a figure swaps:
questions.rationale: The water surface is a horizontal axis: the top of the figure dips to the bottom and vice versa, while left-right positions are untouched.

questions.question: Which of these letters has the SAME mirror image (vertical mirror) as itself?
questions.rationale: The self-mirroring set is A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y - all left-right symmetric. P, L and S all swing their one-sided features to the wrong side.

questions.question: In a mirror, the digit 6 appears as:
questions.rationale: Reflection reverses orientation but is not rotation: 6 becomes a backwards 6. The digit 9 is what you get by ROTATING 6 by 180 degrees - which is why 9 is the standard trap option in mirror questions.

questions.question: A clock seen in a mirror shows 4:30. The actual time is:
questions.rationale: Mirror time = 11:60 - 4:30 = 7:30. Check the shortcut: the two readings sum to 12:00 (4:30 + 7:30), the signature of mirror reflection on a 12-hour dial.

questions.question: The water image of the time 4:30 is:
questions.rationale: Water time = 18:30 - 4:30 = 14:00, which reads 2:00 on a 12-hour dial. The horizontal flip exchanges 12 with 6 and 3 with 9 across the water surface.

questions.question: Applying a mirror reflection and then a water reflection to a figure produces:
questions.rationale: Swapping left-right and then top-bottom turns the figure upside down with left-right restored - exactly a half turn. This identity also explains why rotate-180 options serve as traps in single-reflection questions.

questions.question: The mirror image of the word 'PAN' reads as:
questions.rationale: Two changes happen together: each letter reflects (P, A, N all have one-sided features) AND the letter sequence reverses order. So the result is the letters N-A-P in reversed visual form - not the ordinary spelling NAP.

questions.question: Which digit is unchanged BOTH in a mirror image and in a water image?
questions.rationale: 8 is symmetric both left-right and top-bottom, so neither reflection alters it (0 also qualifies). 3 survives a water flip but not a mirror; 6 and 2 survive neither.

questions.question: In figure-based reflection questions, the fastest elimination strategy is to first check:
options: The most asymmetric detail - arrowheads, dots, tick marks
questions.rationale: A single highly asymmetric element (an arrow pointing up-right, a dot in one corner) appears in a known opposite position in the true reflection - checking it first typically eliminates two or three options instantly. Reflection preserves all sizes and distances, so size checks help only later.
